title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 8:22
body: “Is it then Angels only? No; for hear what follows: "And of His Angels He saith, Which maketh His Angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire: but unto the Son, Thy Throne, O God, is for ever and ever." Behold, the greatest difference!”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “¿Son, pues, solo los ángeles? No; porque oye lo que sigue: "Y ciertamente de los ángeles dice: El que hace á sus ángeles espíritus, y á sus ministros llama de fuego. Mas al hijo: Tu trono, oh Dios, por el siglo del siglo." ¡He aquí la diferencia más grande!”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 11:26
body: “A drought once overtook our city, and all were trembling for the last of evils, and were beseeching God to rid them of this fear. And one might see then that which was spoken of by Moses; (Deut.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Una sequía alcanzó una vez nuestra ciudad, y todos temblaban por el último de los males, y rogaban a Dios que los librara de este miedo. Y entonces se podía ver aquello de lo que habló Moisés; (Deut.”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 12:28
body: “The Rev. Ver., following the Hebrew, has, "And in the pathway thereof (righteousness) there is no death."--G.A.] __________________________________________________________________”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “La Rev. Ver., siguiendo el hebreo, tiene: "En el camino de la justicia está la vida; y la senda de su vereda no es muerte."--G.A.] __________________________________________________________________”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 16:5
body: “Of the lasciviousness and uncleanness which they committed." Now in these words he alludes indeed to fornication; but if one carefully examine the subject, every kind of sin can be called by this name.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “De la lascivia y la inmundicia que cometieron." Ahora bien, en estas palabras alude en verdad a la fornicación; pero si uno examina con cuidado el asunto, toda clase de pecado puede llamarse con este nombre.”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 20:9
body: “Shouldest thou then have gone all lengths in wickedness, yet say unto thyself, God is loving unto men and he desires our salvation: for "though your sins be as scarlet, I will whiten you as snow," (Is.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Aunque hayas llegado a todos los extremos de la maldad, di sin embargo para ti: Dios es amante de los hombres y desea nuestra salvación: porque "si vuestros pecados fueren como la grana, como la nieve serán emblanquecidos" (Is.”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 22:1
body: “Against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who hold the truth in unrighteousness." Here he showeth that the ways of ungodliness are many, and that of truth, one.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans
bodyEs: “Contra toda impiedad é injusticia de los hombres, que detienen la verdad con injusticia." Aquí muestra que los caminos de la impiedad son muchos, y el de la verdad, uno.”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 28:1
body: “This language he employs, not without a purpose, but in consequence of what he had been saying previously; "having girded your loins, having on the breastplate," &c., which are a token of a constant and unceasing advance; for hear what the Prophet saith, "Let it be unto him as the raiment wherewith he covereth himself, and for the girdle wherewith he is girded continually" (Ps.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Este lenguaje lo emplea no sin propósito, sino a consecuencia de lo que había dicho antes: "ceñidos vuestros lomos, teniendo vestida la coraza", etc., que son señal de un avance constante e incesante; porque oye lo que dice el Profeta: "Séale como vestido con que se cubra, y en lugar de cinto con que se ciña siempre" (Sal.”

title: John Chrysostom on Proverbs 31:6
body: “For indeed intemperance in this renders men passionate and violent, and hot-headed, and irritable and savage. Wine has been given us for cheerfulness, not for drunkenness.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Porque en verdad la intemperancia en esto vuelve a los hombres apasionados y violentos, y fogosos, irritables y salvajes. El vino se nos ha dado para la alegría, no para la embriaguez.”
